name: vFlow
what_it_is: High-performance, scalable network flow collector written in Go that ingests IPFIX (RFC7011), sFlow v5, Netflow v5, and Netflow v9 packets and publishes decoded JSON to a message queue. It is designed for enterprise-scale telemetry pipelines with support for replication, dynamic worker scaling, and Prometheus monitoring.
protocols: sFlow v5 raw header and counters (UDP port 6343)
measurement: RESTful stats API (port 8081, format switchable via stats-format config key)
Per-protocol decode counters available via stats endpoint
configuration: YAML config file at /etc/vflow/vflow.conf (path overridable with -config flag)
All keys also settable as CLI flags; CLI takes precedence over file
Per-protocol enable/disable flags: ipfix-enabled, sflow-enabled, netflow5-enabled, netflow9-enabled
Per-protocol worker counts: ipfix-workers (default 200), sflow-workers (default 200), netflow5-workers (default 50), netflow9-workers (default 50)
Per-protocol Kafka topics: vflow.ipfix, vflow.sflow, vflow.netflow5, vflow.netflow9
IPFIX and Netflow v9 template cache files: /tmp/vflow.templates, /tmp/netflow9.templates
IPFIX mirroring to 3rd-party collector via ipfix-mirror-addr and ipfix-mirror-port
Kafka broker set via VFLOW_KAFKA_BROKERS environment variable or brokers key in mq.conf
dynamic-workers: true enables automatic worker scaling
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection mechanism documented
Stress/load generator included under stress/ directory for generating synthetic flow traffic
modes: Default mode: all protocols enabled, Kafka producer enabled
Mirror mode: IPFIX packets replicated to a 3rd-party collector simultaneously
Stats format switchable between prometheus and restful
Producer can be disabled with producer-enabled: false (collect only, no MQ publish)
constraints: Requires an external message queue (Kafka, NSQ, NATS, or rawSocket) to be running before vflow starts; docker-compose uses a 5-second sleep workaround for Kafka readiness
IPFIX and Netflow v9 are template-based protocols; templates must be received before data records can be decoded, and templates are cached to disk for persistence across restarts
UDP packet size defaults to 1500 bytes for all protocols; must be tuned if jumbo frames are used
No built-in authentication or encryption on the UDP listener ports; relies on network-level controls
sFlow type filtering is unsupported by default (sflow-type-filter is empty); all sFlow sample types are processed
docker_services: vflow (image: mehrdadrad/vflow, ports 4739/udp IPFIX, 4729/udp Netflow v9, 6343/udp sFlow, 9996/udp Netflow v5, 8081/tcp stats; depends_on kafka)
prometheus (image: prom/prometheus:latest, port 9090, mounts ./scripts for prometheus.yml)
notable_absences: No TLS/encryption on UDP collection ports
No authentication on the stats/metrics HTTP endpoint
No built-in replay or pcap ingestion capability
No native output to Elasticsearch, Splunk, or syslog without an external consumer
No support for IPFIX over TCP (UDP only)
